notes.meaning: John watches a glorious angel come down from heaven with great power. The angel's heavenly brightness is so dazzling that it lights up the whole earth. This brilliant light shows that God's holy presence is breaking in to expose the darkness of the world.

The angel shouts with a powerful voice that Babylon the great has fallen. The once proud city is turned into a ruined wasteland where only demons, evil spirits, and scavenger birds live. This total ruin fulfills ancient prophecies about the final collapse of God's enemies.

differ.view: Many see Babylon as an end-times world system or city ruled by the Antichrist, a final enemy of Christ. Some think the city will be rebuilt on the Euphrates River.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching holds that Babylon refers to ancient pagan Rome or Jerusalem, rather than the Christian church in Rome.

notes.meaning: Babylon led the nations of the world into moral decay and false worship. Kings joined her in spiritual unfaithfulness, and merchants became wealthy by feeding her greed for luxury. Her corrupt influence reached into government, business, and daily life.

A heavenly voice urges God's people to leave Babylon immediately. Remaining tied to her evil ways would mean sharing in her guilt and suffering her terrible punishment. God always provides a way of escape for those who want to stay faithful to Him.

differ.view: Some evangelicals believe this call is a future warning for believers living during the end-times tribulation to physically escape a rebuilt city of Babylon.

notes.meaning: Babylon's sins have piled up so high that they reach all the way to heaven, like a dark tower. God has not overlooked any of her evil acts. The time has arrived for His justice to respond to centuries of wickedness.

God commands that Babylon receive the full penalty for the pain she caused others. Demanding a double portion is an ancient way of saying that her punishment will be thorough and complete. She will drink from the bitter cup of judgment she once forced upon the world.

Babylon proudly boasted in her heart that she was a reigning queen who would never taste sorrow. Because of her boastful pride and selfish luxury, she is sentenced to an equal amount of agony and grief. Human arrogance cannot protect anyone from God's holy standard.

Terrible plagues of death, famine, and sorrow will strike Babylon suddenly in a single day. Fire will consume her because the Lord God who judges her is all-powerful. No earthly army or fortress can withstand the strength of the Almighty.

The rulers of the earth who indulged in Babylon's sinful luxury break down in tears when they see the smoke of her burning. They realize that their powerful ally and source of pleasure is gone forever. Their sorrow is not over their sin, but over what they have lost.

The kings stand far away because they are terrified of getting caught in her fiery ruin. They cry out in shock that such a mighty and famous world power could fall in just one hour. Earthly strength vanishes the moment God speaks in judgment.

The world's merchants weep and mourn because their biggest buyer has been destroyed. With Babylon gone, there is nobody left to buy their expensive shipments of goods. Their grief comes from the sudden collapse of their own profits.

differ.view: Some note these are luxuries, not needs, and apply 'bodies and souls of men' today to human trafficking and pornography.

notes.meaning: The cargo includes the finest treasures of the ancient world, from gold and silk to spices, wine, and fine horses. Shockingly, the list ends with human bodies and souls, showing that Babylon treated human beings as mere merchandise. God takes note when an economic system values money over human life.

differ.view: Some note these are luxuries, not needs, and apply 'bodies and souls of men' today to human trafficking and pornography.

notes.meaning: The speaker addresses Babylon directly to declare that every luxury she craved is gone forever. All the rich foods and splendid possessions she hoarded have vanished without a trace. Earthly wealth can disappear in a moment and leave the soul completely empty.

The merchants who made fortunes from Babylon keep their distance in terror of her agony. They weep and wail as they watch her burn from afar. Their self-interest keeps them from offering any help to their fallen partner.

The merchants cry out in sorrow over the great city that once dressed in royal purple, fine linen, and gold. They are stunned to see such outward beauty and royal prestige wiped out so quickly. Outward splendor cannot hide inward corruption from God.

Fabulous riches gathered over centuries are wiped away in a single hour. Sea captains, sailors, and ocean travelers stop their ships and watch the blazing disaster from the water. Worldly security proves totally fragile before the judgment of God.

As thick plumes of smoke rise from the burning ruins, the sailors cry out in disbelief. They ask if any city on earth was ever as magnificent and mighty as Babylon. Her unmatched glory has turned into an unmatched disaster.

The seafarers throw dust on their heads as an ancient sign of deep grief and despair. They mourn the fall of the harbor hub that made shipowners wealthy from her vast trade. The suddenness of her destruction leaves the world's traders ruined and helpless.

While worldly traders weep, heaven and God's holy people are told to rejoice. This joy is not petty revenge, but praise because God has brought righteous justice for His persecuted servants. God never forgets the prayers and sufferings of His people.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic writers note that this city killed apostles, so it must be a city of the first century, such as pagan Rome.

notes.meaning: A mighty angel picks up a stone the size of a giant millstone and hurls it violently into the sea. He explains that Babylon will be thrown down just as suddenly and will never be seen again. The vivid picture shows that the city's fall is final and complete.

differ.view: Some say ancient Babylon was never destroyed like this, so the city must one day be rebuilt and then destroyed.

notes.meaning: The music of harps, flutes, and trumpets will go silent in Babylon forever. Skilled workers will no longer practice their crafts, and the cheerful sound of grain being ground will cease entirely. The bustling activity of city life is replaced by complete silence.

differ.view: Some note the Greek word is linked to drugs, and see a kind of addiction to buying, fed by advertising.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic writers point out that these are scenes of ordinary city life, which do not fit Vatican City.

notes.meaning: No household lamp will ever shine again in Babylon, and the happy voices of brides and grooms will never be heard there. Her proud leaders used deceitful sorcery and corrupt charms to lead the whole world astray. Misleading others away from God brings ultimate ruin.

differ.view: Some note the Greek word is linked to drugs, and see a kind of addiction to buying, fed by advertising.

other.view: Catholic writers point out that these are scenes of ordinary city life, which do not fit Vatican City.

notes.meaning: Babylon is held guilty for the shed blood of God's prophets, saints, and all innocent victims killed on the earth. Her final ruin proves that God holds evil powers accountable for the lives they destroy. The Lord hears the cry of the innocent and will make all things right.

differ.view: Some say only a worldwide system, not a single city, could be guilty of all this blood.
